title: PRD
description: What a PM signs: the diagnosis, the whole product's shape, the solution and its scope, requirements with criteria, the surfaces that ship, the MVP line, and how success is measured. The workshop fills it one section at a time from a transcript; the runner owns identity, state, flags and the hash. Compiles to the contract; export freezes it.

doc_status.description: Document status per SPEC §2: draft → reviewed → signed.

baseline.description: Brownfield (R11): the release this PRD is a delta against — null for greenfield.

seed.description: The PM's original idea, as typed.

who.description: Who this is for — specific people in a specific situation, never "users".

problem.description: The pain, timeless: true as long as these people have it, whatever system they use today.

crux.description: The one hardest thing — the obstacle that, solved, makes the rest easier. Empty means the diagnosis is incomplete.

why_now.description: Why this cycle and not six months ago or six months from now.

business_value.description: What it is worth to the business, in terms someone would fund.

evidence.description: Why we believe the problem is real, not assumed — what was observed, counted, or said.

shape.description: The whole product before the line is drawn (R12): what things exist, what states they pass through, who is responsible for what, and where time is cut. Unknowns are recorded with owner `unowned` — expect discovery — never guessed.

lifecycles.description: Every thing in the product that has a life: what it is, the states it passes through in order, and who moves it. Include lifecycles past the MVP line — the line is drawn after this, not before.

subject.description: The thing with the life — an order, a batch, a shift.

states.description: In order, from creation to rest. Terminal states included.

owner.description: The role that moves it between states, or `unowned`.

vocabulary.description: Every term the PRD uses that a stranger could misread, defined once. Requirements and stories are held to these words; a term used but not here is drift.

owner.description: Who decides what this word means, or `unowned`.

attribution.description: For each action that matters later — who did it, and how the product knows. A product that cannot say who recorded what invites the amendment that adds it mid-build.

known_by.description: How the product attributes it — a sign-in, a named device, a shift roster — or `unowned`.

clocks.description: Where time is cut: the boundaries that decide which day, shift, or period something belongs to, and who owns the cut. Midnight is a choice, not a default.

boundary.description: What is being cut — a business day, a shift, a reporting week.

rule.description: Where the cut falls and what decides it.

summary.description: What we are building, one plain paragraph — what it does for the people in `who`, never how it is built.

problem_mapping.description: The line from the solution back to the crux. If it cannot be drawn cleanly, the solution or the problem is wrong.

out_of_scope.description: Anti-requirements with a reason each. An exclusion without a rationale is a boundary, not a strategy.

surfaces.description: The delivery-surface decision: what a person actually gets this cycle. API-only is a decision; silence is not.

kind.description: web app · handheld web app · native app · API · CLI · document.

statement.description: One testable sentence: "A handheld web app a dock lead uses one-handed at the door."

req_refs.description: The requirements whose experience this surface carries. Empty until requirements exist; bound in the requirements section.

deferred.description: Surfaces considered and cut, each with a rationale and the requirements it consciously leaves without a surface.

requirements.description: Atomic, testable, timeless. Ids are sticky — reuse REQ-n for the same requirement across captures; mint new ids only for new requirements.

statement.description: One testable assertion, no rationale, no system names. Functional: what a person can do and what they get.

type.description: Routes the work: functional becomes a story with scenarios; non-functional and constraint become tickets verified by measurement or inspection.

done_definition.description: A yes/no you can answer standing in front of the built system.

acceptance_criteria.description: Each provable by one piece of work, in one place. Lived claims carry numbers.

status.description: Deferred and cut requirements keep their ids and stay in the document.

context.description: System-specific detail the statement must stay free of. Not drift-checked; nothing tests it — behaviour that lives only here is a requirement in disguise.

flags.description: Challenges the PM overrode rather than answered, each named.

mvp.description: The MVP line (R2): drawn after the shape is known, read by every reviewer and judge. The contract binds only what is inside.

line.description: Where the line is, in one sentence a reviewer can quote: what this cycle ships and what it does not.

inside.description: Every committed requirement inside the line.

past.description: What sits past the line — a requirement, a surface, a lifecycle — and why it can wait.

objective.description: Qualitative, durable, aimed at the crux. Not a number, not a feature.

measurements.description: The timeless gauges — no targets, no dates. "Exceptions logged per shift," never "by Q3."

counter.description: What must not get worse while the outcome improves.

key_results.description: This cycle's readings: each bound to one measurement, baseline → target, cycle-stamped, committed or aspirational.

measurement.description: The gauge this reads, quoted from measurements.

target.description: Blank only if tied to an open question with an owner.

commitment.description: Committed: on the hook. Aspirational: a real stretch — certainty means it is sandbagged.

open_questions.description: What engineering will hit that is not yet answered — framed as a question with an owner, never as a product-supplied technical finding.

constraints.description: What product legitimately owns and engineering must live with: regulation, deadlines and the reason behind them, dependencies as facts.

flags.description: Append-only decision history: overrides, kill suggestions, rulings recorded by the doors.

rulings.description: Rulings are spec (R3): a PM's answer made a criterion in one operation — attributed, pinned to the PRD version it landed in, ridden into every writer, reviewer and judge, never re-raised. Append-only; written by the answer door, and by approval when an approved reaction settles its prototype question.

oq.description: The open question this answers, when it answers one.

pq.description: The prototype question this answers, when it answers one.

criterion.description: The acceptance criterion the answer became.

version.description: The PRD version the ruling landed in.

prd_hash.description: The PRD content hash after the ruling landed.

amendment.description: The approved amendment whose reaction settled the question, when approval wrote this ruling.

superseded_by.description: The approved amendment that has since changed the criterion. The ruling stays on the record as history.

amendments.description: Amendments are audited at mint (R4): every proposal carries its blast radius and the vocabulary it introduces, and the PM approves the radius, not just the edit. Append-only; written by the amend door.

target.description: JSON pointer into the PRD's model-facing content.

adds.description: True when the target does not exist yet and the amendment creates it.

from.description: What the target held when the amendment was proposed. Absent when it adds.

origin.description: Where the need came from. Amendments Delivery sends back are the funnel's leak (R8). A workshop amendment is an extraction that contradicted a ruled criterion, held for the PM. A reaction amendment is the specification editor's reading of a PM's reaction to the prototype.

reaction.description: The reaction it was minted from, when its origin is a reaction.

pq.description: The prototype question its reaction answers, when it answers one.

material.description: True when the target is under a drift-checked pointer: approving it moves the hash and bumps the minor version.

radius.description: Everything the change touches, computed at mint and recomputed at approval.

terms.description: Vocabulary terms the changed text uses.

introduces.description: Words the new text uses that the PRD's drift-checked content does not — vocabulary arriving undeclared.

agreements.description: The PM's agreement to an exact revision — the PRD and the prototype built from it — that stories are written from. A later change to either voids it. Append-only; written by the agree door.

prd_hash.description: The PRD content hash the PM agreed to.

prototype_hash.description: The prototype content hash the PM agreed to.

reactions.description: The PM's plain-language reactions to the prototype they were viewing, each with at most one proposed change. While a reaction's amendment is still proposed it holds the backlog and every exit. Outside the content hash; append-only; written by the react door.

pq.description: The prototype question the reaction answers, when it answers one.

seen.description: The revision the PM was viewing.

proposal.description: The amendment proposed for it, or null when the editor judged it presentation only.

screens.description: The prototype screens that show what it targets.

sections.description: Workshop state per section: the session the conversation lives in, turns taken, when it was last extracted.

x-drift-checked.description: The pointers the content hash covers — the spec, not the record around it.
